title: Prospective AI-SC Trial
official: Artificial Intelligence-Selection Committee (AI-SC) Trial: A Prospective Study of Human-AI Collaborative Decision-Making in Liver Transplant Selection
summary: This is a prospective, pre-post implementation study designed to evaluate how artificial intelligence-based selection committee (AI-SC) recommendations affect decision-making when integrated into routine clinical workflows. The study will focus on individual liver transplant candidacy decisions as the primary unit of analysis. Researchers will observe and analyze these decisions during weekly University Health Network (UHN) Liver Transplant Selection Committee meetings over an approximate 12-month period. The goal is to determine if the deployment of AI-SC recommendations changes, optimizes, or influences the committee's final transplant candidacy determinations compared to baseline practices.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* age 18 years or older; undergoing liver transplant assessment at UHN; anticipated discussion at the UHN liver transplant selection committee; ability to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* refusal or withdrawal of consent; cases for which required committee presentation information is unavailable to the study team; cases in which urgent clinical circumstances do not allow the consent process to occur before committee review; cases in which the treating team determines that research contact is inappropriate because of clinical, emotional, or logistical circumstances.

Refusal to participate will not affect transplant assessment, committee review, clinical management, waitlist eligibility, or access to future care.
